card.title: Acknowledge Our History
card.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you box our allotment photo, admit that summer wasn't wasted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We grew three carrots. I need the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got out of bed every morning to water those three carrots with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I could put the photo on my desk at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you? And tell people that part when they laugh at the harvest.

mechanism: A asks B to recognize the shared summer's value beyond its poor harvest and to carry that meaning into displaying the photo.
confusable: Unlike preserving an object for nostalgia alone, A must seek acknowledgment that the lived connection mattered.
comparison: D81-a asks for the story behind three carrots; D81-b asks for handwritten recognition on a retained receipt envelope.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
